intended_object: The quotient K[x]/(x^N) of the coordinate ring K[x] of the additive group 𝔾ₐ over a commutative ring K by the ideal generated by the N-th power of the coordinate x. For N = p^m over a field of characteristic p, this is the coordinate algebra of α_{p^m} (Milne, Algebraic Groups, 2.5). Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
In this library, `additiveGroupCoordinateRing K` is `SymmetricAlgebra K K`. This is the polynomial ring K[x], with the coordinate x = ι(1); the identification is the algebra equivalence `additiveGroupCoordinateAlgEquiv` to `Polynomial K`. `additivePowerIdeal K N` is the ideal generated by x^N. So the definition is exactly K[x]/(x^N), and the same file proves it is K-algebra isomorphic to `AdjoinRoot (X^N)`.

The setting is fully general: any commutative ring K and any natural number N. The degenerate cases behave as expected: for N = 0 the quotient is the zero ring, and for N = 1 it is K.

Mathlib has no dedicated named definition for this quotient. `AdjoinRoot (X ^ N)` is only an isomorphic presentation of it, phrased through the polynomial ring rather than through the additive-group coordinate ring. The definition is not too narrow.

The docstring speaks of a "coordinate ring", but the definition only builds the commutative algebra, with no Hopf-algebra structure. The module documentation says this explicitly, so it is consistent with what the definition is meant to be.
